Dialectical materialism.fact: Dialectical materialism is a philosophy of nature and philosophy of science, developed in the late 19th century based on the writings of Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels. Falsifiability.fact: Popper claimed that induction is not needed in science, that is, he rejected that we learn by the repetition of observations and considered that logical induction was a fallacy. This led Popper's student and collaborator David Miller to write "the mission is to classify truths, not to certify them".

Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages
Falsifiability.question: He cited his encounter with psychoanalysis in the 1910s, especially with _____

Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages
Falsifiability.question: Popper accepted _____'s argument and therefore viewed progress in science as the result of quasi-induction, which is induction without inference rules and which he also called the "path of science"
Falsifiability.fact: David Hume studied how human beings obtain new knowledge that goes beyond known laws and observations, including how to discover new laws. Popper accepted Hume's argument and therefore viewed progress in science as the result of quasi-induction, which is induction without inference rules and which he also called the "path of science".

Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages
Falsifiability.question: In line with _____-Laird's view, Popper proposed an evolutionary mechanism to explain science's success, but he did not consider it part of his epistemology
Falsifiability.fact: Johnson-Laird's view was that "induction is just something that animals, including human beings, do to make life possible". In line with Johnson-Laird's view, Popper proposed an evolutionary mechanism to explain science's success, but he did not consider it part of his epistemology.

Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages
Falsifiability.question: By his own account, because only a negative approach was supported by logic, _____ adopted a negative methodology to prevent the "policy of immunizing our theories against refutation"
Falsifiability.fact: By his own account, because only a negative approach was supported by logic, Popper adopted a negative methodology to prevent the "policy of immunizing our theories against refutation".

Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages
Falsifiability.question: For example, _____ inductive logic is justified by theorems that make explicit assumptions

Falsifiability.fact: For example, the falsifiability of Newton's law of gravitation, as defined by Popper, depends purely on the logical relation it has with a statement such as "The brick fell upwards when released". A brick that falls upwards would not alone falsify Newton's law of gravitation.

Falsifiability.fact: For example, the falsifiability of Newton's law of gravitation, as defined by Popper, depends purely on the logical relation it has with a statement such as "The brick fell upwards when released". A brick that falls upwards would not alone falsify Newton's law of gravitation.

Falsifiability.fact: The methodological part consists, in Popper's view, of informal rules, which are used to formulate hypotheses, accept observations as factual, etc. These include statistical tests: Popper is aware that observation statements are accepted with the help of statistical methods and that these involve methodological decisions.

Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages
Falsifiability.question: These include statistical tests: _____ is aware that observation statements are accepted with the help of statistical methods and that these involve methodological decisions
Falsifiability.fact: The methodological part consists, in Popper's view, of informal rules, which are used to formulate hypotheses, accept observations as factual, etc. These include statistical tests: Popper is aware that observation statements are accepted with the help of statistical methods and that these involve methodological decisions.

Falsifiability.fact: Maxwell said that most scientific laws are metaphysical statements of this kind, which, Popper said, need to be made more precise before they can be indirectly corroborated.

Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages
Falsifiability.question: To refute this, _____ gave the example of an apple that moves from the ground up to a branch and then starts to dance from branch to branch
Falsifiability.fact: To refute this, Popper gave the example of an apple that moves from the ground up to a branch and then starts to dance from branch to branch. According to Popper's definition, this is a basic statement and a potential falsifier for Newton's theory, because the position of the apple at different times can be measured.

Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages
Falsifiability.question: According to _____'s definition, this is a basic statement and a potential falsifier for Newton's theory, because the position of the apple at different times can be measured
Falsifiability.fact: To refute this, Popper gave the example of an apple that moves from the ground up to a branch and then starts to dance from branch to branch. According to Popper's definition, this is a basic statement and a potential falsifier for Newton's theory, because the position of the apple at different times can be measured.

But, for Popper and others, no (falsifiable) law of Natural Selection has been offered, because these tools apply only to certain rare traits.

Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages
Falsifiability.question: "Yet instead of accepting the refutations", _____ wrote, "the followers of Marx re-interpreted both the theory and the evidence in order to make them agree
Falsifiability.fact: In Popper's view, this was both testable and subsequently falsified. "Yet instead of accepting the refutations", Popper wrote, "the followers of Marx re-interpreted both the theory and the evidence in order to make them agree.

Falsifiability.fact: Lakatos described four kinds of falsificationisms: Dogmatic falsificationism – ignores both types of problems.

Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages
Falsifiability.question: Popper responded that _____ was misrepresenting his intellectual history
Falsifiability.fact: Lakatos used dogmatic and naive falsificationism to describe how Popper changed over time and viewed sophisticated falsificationism as his refinement, but also said that Popper sometimes presents as a sophisticated falsificationist. Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages
Falsifiability.question: For example, the statement "Here is a glass of water" goes beyond experience, because the concepts of glass and water "denote physical bodies which exhibit a certain law-like behaviour" (_____)
Falsifiability.fact: Lakatos used dogmatic and naive falsificationism to describe how Popper changed over time and viewed sophisticated falsificationism as his refinement, but also said that Popper sometimes presents as a sophisticated falsificationist. Popper responded that Lakatos was misrepresenting his intellectual history.

Falsifiability.fact: This is sometimes called the 'Duhem–Quine problem'.

Falsifiability.question: An example is _____'s refutation of the theory that celestial bodies are faultless crystal balls

Falsifiability.fact: If the path contradicts Newton's law, it is not clear what should be rejected: Newton's law or the hypothesis that no other body influenced the path. A dogmatic falsificationist would ignore that and consider that Newton's law is falsified.

Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages

Falsifiability.fact: If the path contradicts Newton's law, it is not clear what should be rejected: Newton's law or the hypothesis that no other body influenced the path. A dogmatic falsificationist would ignore that and consider that Newton's law is falsified.

Falsifiability.fact: He wrote that one should nor read Lakatos to understand his intellectual history. A fifth decision is mentioned by Lakatos to allow even more theories to be falsified.

Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages
Falsifiability.question: Later, it was shown that the specific definition proposed by _____ cannot distinguish two false theories, as is the case for all theories in the history of science
Falsifiability.fact: In contradistinction, for Popper, the creative and informal part is guided by methodological rules, which naturally favour theories that are corroborated and have shown their merit over those that are falsified, but this methodology cannot be made rigorous. Popper's way to analyze progress was through verisimilitude, a way to define how close a theory is to the truth, which he did not consider significant, except as an attempt to describe a concept already accepted in practice.

Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages
Falsifiability.question: Popper rejected _____'s explanation and proposed his own mechanism: science progresses by trial and error within an evolutionary epistemology
Falsifiability.fact: Popper rejected Hume's explanation and proposed his own mechanism: science progresses by trial and error within an evolutionary epistemology. Hume believed that his psychological induction process follows laws of nature, but that this does not imply the existence of a method of justification based on logical rules.

Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages

Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages
Falsifiability.question: Therefore, _____ urged Popper to find an inductive principle behind the trial and error learning process and sophisticated falsificationism was his own approach to this challenge
Falsifiability.fact: Lakatos approved Russell's justificationist view. Therefore, Lakatos urged Popper to find an inductive principle behind the trial and error learning process and sophisticated falsificationism was his own approach to this challenge.

Falsifiability.fact: Kuhn, Feyerabend, Musgrave and others mentioned and Lakatos himself acknowledged that this attempt failed, because no normative methodology existed—Lakatos' methodology was anarchy in disguise.

Falsifiability.fact: For example, Watkins wrote "apparently forgetting that he had once said 'Duhem is right [...]', Popper set out to devise potential falsifiers just for Newton's fundamental assumptions".

Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages

Falsifiability.fact: For example, Chalmers pointed out that falsificationists freely admit that observation relies on theory.

Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages

Falsifiability.fact: However, unlike Popper, Lakatos believed that induction was the only alternative to deduction. However, Lakatos' method never provided precise inductive rules.

Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages

Falsifiability.fact: Feyerabend, in Against Method, argued that Lakatos' methodology was essentially epistemological anarchism in disguise, a view echoed by Musgrave.

Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages
Falsifiability.question: Later, _____ noted that Lakatos proposed rules, but these rules did not specify when they must be applied and Feyerabend maintained his position
Falsifiability.fact: In response to critiques from Thomas Kuhn, Paul Feyerabend, and Alan Musgrave, Lakatos admitted that his methodology relied on scientists' judgment. Falsifiability.fact: Stove contended that any observation appearing to contradict Newtonian physics could be explained by other laws or mechanisms, suggesting no truly "non-Newtonian" behavior was possible.
